messages:
Alex: Nightly runner OOM during the long-chat load test. Continuous-batching accounting shows a pad jump ~40% once seq > 1024, and KV cache memory seems to grow in lockstep. Anyone else seeing this?
Mira: Saw a similar spike on my sim yesterday. Perf trace looks like a kernel switch to a fallback that's allocating big temporaries at higher seqs. perf-bot should have the trace.
perf-bot: Perf trace uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/abcd1234 — temp_buf spikes line up with kernel_switch events and batch growth.
Jordan: Can you paste the trace snippet? If the runtime picks the fallback kernel, it can allocate per-batch temp workspace proportional to batch_size * seq_chunk. That + padding explains the jump.
Alex: Snippet from trace log:
```
kernel_choice: fused_fast -> fused_fallback at seq=1280
temp_buf: 1.2GB
kv_cache_resident: 800MB
pad_overhead: 360MB
worker_batch_growth: +3x
```
Tim: Looks like the allocator is rounding workspace allocations to a slab size ~256MB which amplifies waste. Two quick levers: reduce slab granularity for temp buffers, and aggressive buffer reuse/pooling for kernel temps. Also consider lazy KV page materialization for the cache.
Sophia: We tried buffer pooling earlier but hit fragmentation on concurrent batches. Idea: reuse per-seq scratch buffers keyed by sequence length (LRU eviction) so long seqs reuse the same slot instead of allocating new slabs. Also allow a slower kernel that uses less temp memory for high-seq requests — trade CPU for memory.
Mira: Quick numbers from my run: per-seq metadata overhead ~8KB/request, average padding per request ~1.6MB for current batch distribution, but when the worker allows batch growth it bumps average pad per request to ~5MB. So batch growth is the dominant factor here.
Jordan: Proposal: (1) cap worker batch growth to 4x target_slots to limit pad accumulation, (2) maintain a pad_ledger metric and if pad > threshold route to low-memory kernel variant, (3) enable compact_mode allocator for kernel temporaries to reduce slab rounding.
Alex: I'll run an experiment: compact_mode=true, slab_size=64MB, enable_buffer_pool=true. Will run nightly with the same load and post results. If someone can produce a compact repro that triggers the OOM on a small cluster that'd speed iteration.
Tim: I'll spin up a repro harness: 1k concurrent chat flows with seq up to 2048 and staggered arrival to simulate real batching. Example run for tracing:
```
./run_test --clients 1000 --max-seq 2048 --trace-kernels --mem-account > trace.log
```
Mira: :thumbsup: I'll run that trace and add a new metric for `kv_shadow_pages` to check if KV pages are being double-counted during reorder/commit. Could be an accounting bug.
perf-bot: Alert recorded: nightly-runner OOM (thread 1803456789). Investigators assigned: Alex, Tim, Mira, Jordan, Sophia.
